content.user_title: Analyze Competitors and Prioritize Market Opportunities
content.value_statement: Competitor strategy is difficult to compare when evidence comes from different tools and formats. This skill organizes SEO, content, backlink, technical, and AI citation evidence into prioritized opportunities and a phased action plan.
actual_capabilities: Classifies direct competitors, indirect alternatives, and content competitors.
Benchmarks three to five domains across keywords, backlinks, traffic, content, and technical SEO.
Evaluates AI citation patterns and identifies topics competitors do not cover well.
Labels every metric as Measured, User-provided, Estimated, or N/A.
Produces comparison tables, evidence-based strengths and weaknesses, and a phased action plan.
Provides templates for competitor profiles, synthesis reports, positioning analysis, and battlecards.
limitations: Reliable results require competitor URLs, business context, exports, or supported research tools.
Tool-free traffic, authority, ranking, and backlink metrics may remain estimates or N/A.
The skill does not produce the dedicated pairwise topic map handled by content-gap analysis.
Optional web retrieval depends on a host-provided Firecrawl connector and network access.

use_cases.title: Set quarterly SEO priorities
use_cases.description: Benchmark three to five domains across rankings, content, backlinks, technical SEO, and AI citations before setting quarterly priorities.

use_cases.title: Build an evidence-based battlecard
use_cases.description: Convert competitor positioning, pricing, strengths, and weaknesses into an evidence-based battlecard for sales and messaging teams.

use_cases.title: Assess a new market
use_cases.description: Identify direct and indirect competitors, evaluate the market, and choose immediate, short-term, and long-term opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Review one competitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with one known competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the SEO strategy for [competitor URL]. Label each metric as Measured, User-provided, Estimated, or N/A. Cite the source for every claim.

prompt_templates.title: Compare several domains
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [my site] with [competitor 1], [competitor 2], and [competitor 3]. Build one table covering traffic, authority, rankings, backlinks, and content cadence. Prioritize five opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate multichannel strengths
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced SEO, video, and AI citation review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [competitor] across content, technical SEO, backlink assets, YouTube outliers, and AI citations. Explain each repeatable strength and exploitable weakness using labeled evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a strategic landscape
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced market analysis with positioning and execution planning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a competitive landscape for [market] using [competitors] and [our data]. Separate direct, indirect, and content competitors. Apply a positioning framework, quantify confidence, and produce a phased action plan with owners and evidence gaps.

output_examples.input: Compare our analytics platform with three named competitors and prioritize SEO opportunities.
output: Executive summary: Competitor A leads on authority and backlinks, while Competitor B has stronger publishing velocity.
Priority opportunity: Build evidence-rich comparison pages for commercial terms where competitors rank and your site does not.
Action plan: Validate keyword volumes now, publish two pages this month, and review ranking movement after eight weeks.

output_examples.input: Create a battlecard for one enterprise competitor using current public evidence.
output: Battlecard finding: The competitor emphasizes integrations, but public pricing and onboarding evidence remain incomplete.
Recommended response: Lead with faster implementation and transparent cost only after validating both claims with current sources.

output_examples.input: Assess a video-heavy competitor and identify SEO and AI citation openings.
output: Observed strength: Video outliers cluster around beginner questions and use consistent outcome-led titles.
Opening: Publish cited definitions and supporting videos for high-intent questions that lack complete competitor coverage.

best_practices: Provide target domains, your site, market, audience, and available exports before analysis.
Keep metric labels, source links, and source dates visible in every comparison.
Validate estimated claims before using them in sales, investment, or publishing decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not present model estimates as measured data.
Do not compare unrelated companies without separating direct, indirect, and content competitors.
Do not scrape restricted pages or bypass access controls.

faq.question: How many competitors should I include?
faq.answer: Use three to five close competitors for the main benchmark. Record additional companies for later review.

faq.question: Do I need an SEO platform?
faq.answer: No. Without tools or exports, unavailable metrics must be labeled Estimated or N/A.

faq.question: Can the skill retrieve competitor pages?
faq.answer: It can use an optional Firecrawl connector when the host provides it. Network access and connector execution should require user approval.

faq.question: Does it replace content-gap analysis?
faq.answer: No. Use the dedicated content-gap workflow for a pairwise map of missing topics sorted by traffic potential.

faq.question: What does the final report contain?
faq.answer: It contains an executive summary, comparison table, evidence-based findings, priority opportunities, and an immediate, short-term, and long-term action plan.

faq.question: How does it prevent unsupported claims?
faq.answer: Every metric receives an evidence label. Missing required data is marked N/A instead of being invented.
